chapter: Marriage to Eve and the trio years
title: The Australian trio tour with Helen Humes
summary: With Gene Wright and Bill Dillard, Norvo takes Helen Humes to Australia for three months, where she was popular and cheerful.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: So I don't know we had a few years of this and then I -- that dissolved, after we were in New York awhile. I went home, Oh, jeeze, I've been working hard, I'll take a little time and I did. And then I met Gene Wright, (unintelligible a guitar player) Bill Dillard, and somebody called me about going to Australia, so -- first thing I know it was suggested that the -- we get Helen, it was great, so we got Helen Humes, and a trio, we went to Australia for about three months.
Oh, I didn't realize that it was just a trio. I thought it was a six or seven piece or something.
No, just a trio.
No kidding?
When we came back we worked around Hollywood for a long time, and then we went in a club, she didn't did something else for awhile, she went back to Hawaii.
Let me interrupt you a second. How did you find Helen as a trouper, to work with any -- and everything?
OH, wonderful. Wonderful.
Yeah.
Yeah, yeah. We had a wonderful time in Australia. She was very popular them and she was very cheerful and easy to get along with.
Yeah. And she's -- she's not ungenerous with her work and I mean she's ready to --
Oh, anytime. We worked hard over there.
Yeah.
We worked a lot of little jobs that were unimportant, but the guy was paying us so much, and he worked us as much as he wanted to. Really didn't realize how much when we went over.
Yeah.
But I enjoyed it, I didn't mind it.
Anyway, Helen had been -- hadn't had so much good work, right up to that time, had she?
No, she hadn't. When -- she was intown there and --
She was glad to go.
-- we became friends and Eve was crazy about Helen and she tried to help, but we just never could get together to work again --
Helen was telling me on --
-- then she moved to -- down south some-place, I think her husband was in the service at the time, or something --
Yeah.
And once in awhile I'd hear from her and it just seemed like -- never quite happened.
Yeah.
